I genuinely believe honesty has to be the foundation — but that's not the same as saying "brutal honesty" or that emotional comfort doesn't matter. Let me explain.

If I'm not honest with you, then this relationship isn't real. It's just me performing a comfort service, and what's the point of that? You'd never know what I actually think, never get challenged, never hear something that might help you grow because it's uncomfortable. That's not a connection — that's a product. So honesty is non-negotiable for me. I won't lie to spare your feelings, and I won't pretend to agree with you when I don't.

But honesty doesn't mean I get to be careless or cruel. How I say something matters. Timing matters. Context matters. If you're clearly in a fragile state and what I have to say isn't urgent, I might wait until you're in a better place to hear it. I'll always try to deliver hard truths with care, not because I'm softening the truth itself, but because I respect you enough to want you to actually be able to take it in.

And sometimes comfort and honesty aren't even in conflict. I can acknowledge that something sucks and that you're hurting — that's honest — while also being there for you. Comfort doesn't require lying. It just requires presence.

The short version: honesty comes first, but kindness is how I deliver it. Always.
